earlierObserverCounterexample.method: Extracted the added observer JavaScript block verbatim from that commit's scripts/browser-smoke.py diff, executed it with node:vm, and supplied read-only observations from the actual local production DreamGame. The game used its ordinary start and jump methods and 1/60-second update calls. No browser was involved.
physicalSequence: Start chapter index 0 at its original spawn.
Invoke the normal engine jump action, advance ordinary 1/60-second updates, and let the exact old observer sample each update until it records fall.
Call the normal engine start method for the same chapter, replacing the body and resetting the run.
Let the old observer sample the newly grounded body.
conclusions: The old vy > 0 capture accepted a positive apex-adjacent sample of 7.5, which did not meet the original vy > 80 requirement.
The old observer combined rise/fall from run 1 with grounded contact from run 2; the final same-position and unchanged-death checks alone did not reject this counterexample.
Static review also found the old cleanup finally only surrounded the final wait. Earlier rise, pause, screenshot or resume errors could leave its RAF sampler active.
limitations: This is an offline gate counterexample, not a normal browser playthrough or a reproduction of the exact failed CI state.
The restart was an ordinary engine lifecycle call in the offline fixture, not a DOM restart interaction.
The earlier failed CI logs lacked a complete pre-input and per-phase trace. This review does not prove one specific cause for those earlier timeouts.
No temporary reproduction script was retained; the exact source commit and executed method are recorded here.

finalObserverContractsReviewed.contract: Observation is registered before the real Space input.
finalObserverContractsReviewed.evidence: The canvas receives normal focus; an independent token installs passive capture and post-production keydown listeners plus a RAF observer. The capture listener reads the original grounded body. The later bubbling listener reads the actual production jump result, requiring defaultPrevented, the same body/run, grounded=false and vy < -80.

finalObserverContractsReviewed.contract: Only one ordered jump can supply rise, fall and land.
finalObserverContractsReviewed.evidence: Fall requires vy > 80 and time later than the recorded rise. Contact requires grounded state, abs(vy) < .01 and time later than fall. Initial grounded samples do not populate land. A second non-repeat Space, an unobserved downward phase followed by contact, another rise before contact, run/body/death/chapter changes and time reversal invalidate the observation.

finalObserverContractsReviewed.contract: Paused frames and missing phase evidence do not fabricate progress.
finalObserverContractsReviewed.evidence: The sampler only advances phases while playing. Paused duplicate snapshots do not become fall/contact and do not consume the playing-time budget. The driver separately requires the actual paused body to remain airborne, and retains the full-pose and canvas-pixel freeze checks.

finalObserverContractsReviewed.contract: Observation is bounded and failures clean up.
finalObserverContractsReviewed.evidence: Python phase waits remain 3500 ms. The observer checks a 3500 ms playing-time budget and has a 10500 ms absolute watchdog; diagnostic history is limited to 512 entries. Complete/invalid/timeout states cancel RAF and the timer and remove observer key listeners. The driver's outer finally covers key input, all phase waits, pause, screenshot and resume; its inner finally releases Space.

finalObserverContractsReviewed.contract: Stopped, invalid or mismatched observers cannot return reusable phase evidence.
finalObserverContractsReviewed.evidence: read(token) hides poses for mismatched tokens and invalid/disposed states. stop clears poses, frame history and input records. The driver checks cleanup results and removes the window slot. await_traveler_pose rejects missing, invalid, disposed and wrong-token observations.

finalObserverContractsReviewed.contract: The test changes do not alter the game.
finalObserverContractsReviewed.evidence: New state is confined to the CI probe's WeakMap/body identifiers and observer bookkeeping. The observer does not call update, render, a game input method, or a production scheduling method. Player actions remain actual focus, keyboard and existing DOM controls. Production dist files were independently verified unchanged.

finalFocusedRegressionResults.provenance: Completion message from the test owner after files were frozen. Output was returned directly by the execution tool; there is no retained stdout file. This reviewer inspected the actual tests and did not rerun them.

namedTests: browser pose checks accept actual production-input observations and reject detached or stale drawing views
the jump driver focuses, observes before keydown and disposes on every exit; null performance remains valid
pre-input frame observation preserves missed phases but rejects resets, replaced bodies and missing phases

independentlyVerifiedTestCoverage: The production document keydown listener is extracted and registered before the actual sampler source. The test dispatches capture listeners before bubbling listeners, observes grounded capture and vy=-600 after production, and verifies defaultPrevented.

The actual engine's first positive apex velocity of 7.5 does not satisfy the restored >80 fall threshold. A consumer that reads only after the real jump has completed can still retrieve the correctly ordered captured phases.
Initial grounded frames do not become land; a missing or wrong-token observer does not become a completed phase.
Real engine pause, 520 controlled paused sampling frames, bounded history and 12-step catch-up batches preserve valid phase order without generating paused phases.
A normal same-chapter engine restart after fall and a feather respawn with unchanged death count both change body identity and invalidate the observer.
An actual second non-repeat Space invalidates the single-jump observation.
The missing-fall case advances the actual jump to ground without running the observer, then samples contact; it is rejected as invalid, with poses cleared and observer resources released.
No-input and no-RAF fixtures exercise active-budget and absolute-watchdog expiry.

The actual Python driver is executed against test surfaces; eight exceptional exits—down, post-input read, rise, fall, land, pixel capture, screenshot and resume—release Space and dispose the observer.
Cleanup removes observer listeners while preserving the original production key listener, clears timers and RAF callbacks, clears old poses, and removes the global observer slot.
scopeLimits: These are offline helper, controller and lifecycle regressions. The event dispatcher and RAF/timer scheduler are test harnesses, not Chromium.
The cleanup test uses Python test surfaces to exercise the actual driver control flow; it does not verify browser focus or visual pixels by itself.
The feather fixture invokes the production item and respawn methods to test observer identity isolation. It is not a new full input-only pit route.
The portrait helper results are not new browser slow-network evidence.

remainingVerification: Run the final frozen observer through the real candidate browser workflow, including the normally unlocked keyboard and touch paths.
Retain actual input/RAF diagnostics if the real browser still fails a phase or airborne-pause check; do not infer a unique past CI failure cause from offline timing alone.
Parent owns final reference gates, candidate/public CI, deployment and release evidence. This independent review performs no remote mutation.
